about: Céilí's finishing pass on Study 4, read by scripts/build_original_study.py for Céilí only. The judged corrections are drawing and spacing decisions that the prints support but do not settle. The finish is noise clean-up, kept within about two units of the drawing.

sit_on_baseline.h: The h stood 40 units above the baseline in Studies 2 to 4, from the frame of the N45 h. Both prints set it on its line. N46 prints its feet level with i, e and d.alt1 (1508 px), and on N45 it stands no higher than its neighbours i and j. Its ascender (803) also stood 40 units above k (767) and l (759). Placement on a paste-up is setting, not drawing, so the h sits on the baseline like n and m.

pen_terminals: A broad pen cuts a stroke straight, with two sharp corners. N45 and N44 print the cuts crisp, N46's toner rounds them, and the mean of the two prints domes the cut and rounds both corners (c, e, e.alt1, t, a.alt1, f, g, p, x, z, the ampersand, the parentheses, 3, 4, 5, 7 and ?). Where a stroke end turns at least 150 degrees within 120 units through two corners, the cut is drawn straight through the middle of the drawn one and the stroke's edges run on to meet it. The feet of upright stems stay rounded, as every print draws those of n and m. This is done only where each new corner lies within 9 units (about a source pixel) of the drawn outline and the straight cut lies within 6 units of the drawn one.

pen_diamond.why: The dots of ! and ? came out as rounded diamonds whose sides bulge, so that each corner turns only about 30 degrees. N46 rounds them, while N45 and B2 print sharp pen diamonds with near-straight sides. Each dot is now the face's period (the N45 pen diamond), mapped by the affine that best takes its four corners onto the dot's. The dot keeps its printed corners, and with them its place and its gap to the stroke. Its weight, 6 to 16% above the period's, comes down to the period's.

bold_dot_gap.why: The Bold set the dots of ! and ? 7 and 10 units from their strokes (F_PASS of the Regular's gap), and the Bold Italic 5 and 8, close enough to read as joined at text sizes. The Bold now keeps the whole of the Regular's gap, cut along the midline, and the Bold Italic 1.3 of it, since the slope's extra weight takes some of it back.

double_acute.why: The double acute (a modern construction from the fada) set its two strokes 14 units apart in the Regular, 9 in the Italic, 6 in the Bold and 3 in the Bold Italic, all but touching. Every style now keeps them about 14 units apart (the sloped styles allow for the growth that follows).

quote_kerning.why: The release's kerning measured letter and quote only where they share a height. A letter whose top just reached the quote's foot was kerned by up to 150 units, and its neighbour not at all: o’ -150 but e’ 0, ’a -150 but ’e 0, d’ -85 but m’ 0. One rule now holds for every letter: the quote stands 0.65 of the n|n gap clear of the letter's upper part, measured from 0.55 x-height up.

finish.what: Done by scripts/ceili_finish.py. In the Regular's traced letters, before the bold and sloped styles are derived, three things change. A curve that left a stem on a handle too short for its bend (a corner hidden in a smooth node, as at the shoulders of n, m and h) now leaves on the stem's tangent, within 3 units. A corner drawn as a cluster of short pieces becomes one corner, within 6 units. A node that one curve can replace within 2 units goes. Every glyph of every style, before accented letters are composed, gets the same tidying: rounding specks are folded away, and the bold's reopened joins (traced from a raster as runs of short lines) are drawn as curves. Corner clusters become one corner, extremes get nodes (again after the slope's shear) and redundant nodes are removed, all within 1.5 units. No step may join pieces or open or close a counter; where one would, the glyph keeps its outline from before that step (so the Bold Italic yen, whose narrow opening the slope's growth closed, is only narrowed there).

second_pass.about: A second review of the finished fonts found seven defects; each is corrected by one rule (scripts/ceili_finish.py), applied by build_original_study.py to the finished candidate only. Measurements are font units, from the fonts before and after.

stems.why: Noise: the h's stems were 100 and 99 beside n's 108 and 113, m's 115, 110 and 109 and i's 106, so the h read light in every style (Bold 159 against n's 168 and 173). The prints settle no weight finer than a source pixel (about 9 units), so each straight stem is given the face's stem, 108 (the builder's, from l and n), by moving its two edges, at most 4 units each; the derived styles follow.

bold_heavy_strokes.why: The bold's pen grows level strokes by its small vertical radius, right for the face's thin horizontals but not for the few level strokes drawn at least 0.75 of a stem in the Regular: the 7's bar went 93 to 102 and the 3's 91 to 101 while the 1's stem went 102 to 162, so 1977 read as a Regular 7 among bold figures, and the hyphen 81 to 91 (the dashes, + - = and # follow it). These take the stems' gain, 1.5 (the 7's bar 139, the hyphen and dashes 120, + - = 121, # 103): the bar's lower edge comes down, the pen's cut and the diagonal running on along their own lines, and the hyphen grows about its axis. The letters' crossbars (ð đ ħ ł ŧ, and the bars of € and ¥) keep the pen's weight, as t's and f's own do, and so do the rings of @ © ® ¤ °, which the rules' weight would close (@ joined its a, ° kept 28% of its counter).

bold_joins.why: The bold reopened the open joins of b, d, k, p, r and 9 as a channel along the middle of the Regular's passage, taking from both sides: p's stem narrowed from 166 to 141 at the join and k's from 165 to 142, and the cracks were 12 to 18 units in the Bold and 4 to 10 in the Bold Italic. Each stem now keeps the edge the pen gives it, and the arm, leg or bowl that comes back to it is cut back along one curve parallel to that edge, to stand at least 15 units clear (F_PASS of the Regular's opening where that is wider), in the Bold and again after the Bold Italic's hair of weight. A crack under close_under units that cuts a counter off is closed instead, as the Bold's 6 is: the ampersand's tail stood 8 units over its bar in both bold styles, and the yen's curl 4 and 6 units from its arm. The joins now stand 16 to 22 units open in both bold styles (the Bold Italic's were 4 to 14).

bold_dot_feet.why: The bold's pen, mitred at the sharp foot of the pen-diamond dots, ran the ! dot 11 units below the Regular's, so the ! fell outside the baseline snap and sat 25 units low (stroke top 629, dot bottom -33, against the Regular's 643 and -8). The dots now reach down only as far as the Regular's, so ! and ? stand where the Regular's stand, their gaps unchanged.

quote_over_foot.why: The quote rule measures only the letter's upper part, so after l (and L, ł) it pulled the quote in over the long foot to -345, 64 units from the stem, where it read as the apostrophe of ľ. A quote may still tuck in over a letter's lower part but never stands wholly over it: its far edge reaches at least the part's tip, so the quote's head stands over the foot's tip: l’ is -205 (Italic -200, Bold -255, Bold Italic -250), the quote 202 units from the Regular's stem.

bar_spacing.why: The spacing saw the bars of ð and đ only where they dipped into the x-height zone, so the Regular's ð kept d's advance with its bar hanging 90 units into the letter before (đ 96), while the Bold's was set 130 wider than d. Both are now spaced as d by one rule in every style: d's sidebearings, the bar's overhang added to the advance, and the bar's end no further left than -20 (the Regular's ð 722 wide, the Bold's 837).

currency.why: € was drawn 1.12 x-heights tall (602) and ¥ at the symbols' 1.05 (565), against the figures' 538 (0 and £). € now spans the zero (-8 to 538, its round overshoot) and ¥ stands from the baseline to the £'s height; both keep the release's construction, and the bold ¥ no longer dips 16 units below the baseline.

bold_section.why: The bold drew § at the weight halfway between the styles that it gives superiors and fractions, so it went 85 to 94 while s went 91 to 123. It is a full-size sign: it now takes the bold's stem, 120 (measured as those were).

third_pass.about: A third review of the finished fonts found six defects; each is corrected by one rule (scripts/ceili_finish.py), applied by build_original_study.py to the finished candidate only. Measurements are font units, from the fonts before and after.

math_signs.why: The bold set its math signs out from its own rule weight (symbols.make_symbols places each piece a multiple of the rule's weight from the axis), so when the second pass made the rules heavier (81 to 121) the pieces moved apart instead of growing in place: = stood 157 between its bars against the Regular's 105, the bar of ± dropped to -121..0 (Regular -37..44), that of ≤ and ≥ to -67..54 (17..98), ÷ ran from -40 to 576, over the 538 x-height (Regular 44..492), ≈ stood 221 apart (175), and ~ and ^ grew upward only (215..382 to 215..420, 350..602 to 350..641). Each piece keeps the second pass's weight and now grows about its Regular counterpart's centre. The white beside a rule stays the Regular's: = 105 about the 268 axis (95..442), ≈ 175, and the underbars of ± ≤ ≥ as far under the plus and the chevron as in the Regular (± -77..598, ≤ ≥ -43..528), so each underbar lies within the Regular's reach plus the growth of the pieces above it. The dots of ÷ are the Regular's drawn with the bold's pen, about their own centres (28..509); kept at the Regular's white they would touch the x-height and the baseline. ~ and ^ stand about their own centres (195..401, 331..622). + − × < > ¬ and the slash of ≠ already grew in place.

quote_near_piece.why: The second pass's rule (a quote may tuck in over a letter's lower part but its far edge reaches at least the part's tip) measured the far edge of the whole double quote, so ” could tuck its first comma in over l's foot as far as ’ had before the rule: l” and L” stayed kerned -345, -330, -350 and -350 (Regular, Italic, Bold, Bold Italic) with the comma 64, 64, 69 and 52 units from the stem, where it read as ľ”, and ł” -260 to -280. The far edge is now that of the quote's piece nearest the letter, so a double quote tucks in exactly as far as a single one: l”, L” and ł” are -205, -200, -255 and -250, as l’ is. The same floor now also holds for ‘ and “ after a letter, which the builder's own kerning sets (none of those pairs reached over a foot); ' " ‚ „ ‹ › « » are not kerned after letters. ľ” in the Regular and Italic now takes l”'s kern, the ” 78 and 71 units clear of ľ's own apostrophe (it was 58 and 56); in the bolds it keeps its exception (-195, -185), which stands the ” 47 units, 0.6 of the n|n white, clear of the apostrophe, as the quote rule stands every quote clear of a letter's upper part.

small_signs.why: The bold's small signs barely gained weight: the bullet was the Regular's outline (ink 1.000 of the Regular's), and % ‰ @ ® ™ ¹²³ ½¼¾ ª º gained 8 to 34% of ink where the letters gain 52% (stem 108 to 169). The bullet is now the Regular's disc drawn with the bold's pen (ink 1.47). % and ‰, which the bold drew at the halfway weight it gives superiors, take the bold's stem as § does (median stroke 58 to 85, ink 1.58), and so do the c of © (stem 71 to 110) and the a of @ (102 to 147), the a made a little smaller where it must be to keep the white the release's a had inside its ring (at the whole stem alone it met the ring). The superiors, fractions, ordinals, ™ and the r of ® are drawn at small_weight of the way from the Regular's stem to the bold's (symbols.make_symbols, SMALL_GLYPH_WEIGHT; the release's 0.5): the heaviest weight, tried from 0.5 to 1.0 in the Bold and in the Bold Italic narrowed and grown as the builder does, at which every counter keeps at least 0.40 of the Regular's area and 0.64 of its inscribed radius (the bold's own floors are 0.36 and 0.55) and every opening at least 0.61 of its width. At 0.8 the 4's small counter in ¼ and ¾ fell to 0.37 of its area in the Bold Italic and at 1.0 to 0.23. Their ink is now 1.36 to 1.43 of the Regular's (¹ stem 75 to 106). At the whole stem the r of ®, the bold r made small, closes its open join into a counter in the Bold Italic, so it is drawn at small_weight too (stem 67 to 84, the release's 78). The rings of © ® @ ° ¤ keep the pen's weight (a later pass on all four faces).

settle.why: Rounding an outline to whole units turns its short handles: the drawing (before rounding) has no kinked smooth joins, but the Italic m came out with 8-degree joins at its arches and clusters of 10 to 14 degree joins at its feet, where pathops had chopped the sheared curves at x-extremes a unit or two from the corners into pieces 2 to 5 units long, and the h's shoulder met its right stem in a 5-degree kink (Bold 12) where a 6.7-unit handle was rounded. Base letters and figures with a kink of 5 degrees or more: Regular 37, Italic 53, Bold 43, Bold Italic 56 (all glyphs 164, 230, 169, 242). Each outline is now put on the grid once, from the drawing as it stood before rounding (the sloped styles' after the shear): nodes only at extremes the curve passes by more than a unit, the redundant nodes the shear leaves removed, every node rounded and each handle set at the whole-unit place nearest its exact direction, a little longer where that points it truer; at a join the drawing makes smooth both handles take the join's one tangent. The result is kept only if it keeps the glyph's pieces and counters, does not overlap itself, leaves no extreme without a node and no run of facets, and lies within keep units of the drawing and cap of the release's ink (which had itself strayed up to 3.6 units from the drawing in the Bold Italic). In the Bold Italic 314 of 315 outlines were settled, at most 1.49 units from the drawing and 1.88 from the release. m, n and h are now free of kinks in every style; base letters and figures with a kink of 5 degrees or more: Regular 23, Italic 22, Bold 29, Bold Italic 31 (all glyphs 74, 87, 124, 130). What remains are the drawing's own shallow corners (the b's open join, a pen cut), which are drawn as corners.

straight_feet.why: The second pass gave the stems the face's weight by moving their straight edges, but h's left edge still bulged out below its line: 87 above y 160, 78 at y 90 and 82 at y 40 (Bold 80, 71 and 75), the prints' mean (Study 4 has the same bulge), where n, m and k run straight to their feet. Every evened stem (f h i j k l.alt1 m n p r r.alt1 s.alt1 1 4, and with them their accented forms) is checked: where an edge, below its straight line, bulges out past the line by more than `least` units and comes back to the foot's corner, the line is carried on down to the corner. A foot that flares out to its corner (l.alt1's, f's into its foot stroke) is drawn so. Only h (9 units) and r.alt1 (3 at the foot of its descender, 4 at its right stem) qualified: the h's left edge now runs at 86 from its top to its foot (Bold 78); h and r.alt1 are one unit narrower, as their spacing now sees them.

j_bar.why: j's bar stood 22 units above its stem against i's 31 (closest points; Italic 22 and 30, Bold 11 and 20, Bold Italic 10 and 18), so the j read as dotted closer than the i. j's bar is moved up to stand as far from its stem as i's, in the Regular before anything is derived from it and again in the bold once its pen has drawn both: 31, 30, 19 and 19 against i's 31, 30, 20 and 18. The ij follows; ĵ is the dotless j with a circumflex and is not built this way.

fifth_pass.about: A fourth independent review of the released fonts (font outlines only) found three defects shared by the four faces. Each is corrected by one rule for all of them, in scripts/symbols.py (approx_sign, ring_weight, ring_letters, heavier_ring) and scripts/build2.py (Font2.stack_anchors, bottom_clear, the mark and mkmk features), switched on for the release by scripts/build_candidate.py (APPROX_WHITE, RING_SHARE, MARK_STACKS); the study fonts do not change. Measurements are font units, from the fonts before and after.

approxequal.why: ≈ stood 395 tall (71..466) against the ='s 267 (135..402), its waves 65 heavy against bars of 81 and 126 apart against the ='s 105, and the third pass kept that design in the bold (97 against 121, 463 tall); its waves are now drawn at the bars' weight (80.5, Italic 81.5, Bold 120, Bold Italic 121), centred on the bars on the 268.5 axis, 0.7 of the ='s white apart (73): 317 tall (110..427; Bold 393, 72..465)

rings.why: the rings of © ® @ ° ¤ were drawn at the pen's hairline, 36 to 58 (Bold 41 to 64), beside an o whose heavier side is 124 (Bold 185); the review asked for half the o and no counter closes at it, so each ring is now at least that, 63 (Italic 67 to 68, Bold 94 to 95, Bold Italic 99 to 100), a departure from the pen-weight design (README, the fifth pass); © and ® grow from 565 to 584 tall (Italic 587, Bold 634, Bold Italic 656, where the r's 12-unit crack may not narrow), the Bold Italic @'s a, 4 from its ring, now 18 clear; ° keeps a counter of 64 (89 before; Bold 79), ¤ one of 238 (269; Bold 176)
rings.final_review: the final review found the figure-size signs outgrown: © and ® up to 656 tall against the figures' 565 and the Bold's ° 162 to 269 tall, twice the bullet. © and ® keep the figures' height with a ring of 0.4 of the o grown inward, 51 (Italic 54), the c and r drawn 0.95 to 1.0 as large; in the bolds the r, whose 12 to 14-unit mouth the slope and the grid would shut if it were drawn smaller, holds the ring to the white it leaves, 66 (Bold Italic 61). ° is no taller than 0.3 of the figures, 170, its ring 51 to 56 and its counter as wide, 57 to 59 (symbols.held_ring, heavier_ring)

marks.why: no mkmk (x + circumflex + acute: 140 into each other), no anchor on a precomposed letter, the comma below ran through j's and g's descenders (90 and 26 into them), the bold's g took its top marks 42 above (Bold Italic 40) against ĝ's 48, and U+0323 had no glyph; now top marks stand 47 to 48 clear (Bold g 47, Bold Italic 52), stacks 48 apart, comma and dot below at least 21 clear; one rule in every face: the dot above (U+0307) keeps the anchor the ponc is set by, so ḃ ċ ḋ ḟ ġ ṁ ṗ ṡ ṫ and every base + U+0307 shape exactly as before; every other top mark takes the place the face's accents take on its letters (not the ponc's), raised where the letter's own ink comes closer than the face's accent gap (the white of the precomposed vowels); each precomposed letter carries top, ponc and bottom anchors of its own, so a mark typed after it stands on its accent; an mkmk feature sets a second mark above (or below) the first, the same gap apart; a comma or dot below moves along the line, then down, until it stands clear of a descender; U+0323 (combining dot below) is added, the face's dot

insular_r_comma.why: ŗ with the insular r (ss01) hangs its comma under the r's descender, and the bold's pen brought the two within 6.1 units (Bold) and 0.8 (Bold Italic); the comma now moves along the line until it stands at least the comma's gap (0.06 x-height) clear, 34.0 and 32.3; the Regular's 50.1 and the Italic's 43.3 are unchanged

changed.why: every glyph whose outline differs from the fourth pass's fonts, per style (with the added dotbelowcomb); kerning changes only in pairs with one of them, the builder's own method applied to the new shapes; the line box, names and every other outline are unchanged
